explanation: Fires most on operator/punctuation tokens inside synthetic math word problems, especially ' =' after 'Solve ... +k' and '(-' after a division sign; also scattered high hits on unrelated tokens in prose and code (e.g. 'real-time', 'accredited', ' do', namespace ';', '{'). Outside math the firing is unpredictable.

Fires on the first token (or first subword) of a person's given name, especially when a full name begins in running text after a verb or preposition ('said Rh|onda', 'married Norm|a', 'coached by Dan'). Weaker on surnames, place names, or names that are already well established in context.

Fires on structural words in templated math problems, most strongly ' be' in 'Let x be ...', and also 'Suppose', 'Solve' and 'Calculate the remainder'. Also fires on statistical/LaTeX notation tokens ('SD', '\to', 'mathbf'). Weak on ordinary prose.

Fires on the token right after a 'sur'/'suf'/'sup'/'sum'-like prefix: 'suffer/suffering/suffered', 'Sur|ratt', 'sur|rogated', 'Sur|rounded', 'immunosup|pressive', 'S|umer'. The strongest hits are subword continuations after 'Sur'/'sur'; whole-word 'suffer' sits at a steady moderate level.

A mixed bag: tokens inside non-Latin scripts and broken byte-encoded characters (Japanese, Hindi), code/doc markup tokens ('@version', '@file', '\~', box-drawing characters, email domains, C++ stream '<<'). No single shared feature. Ordinary English prose gives weak activation.

Fires on content nouns or function words in formulaic, boilerplate-like text: legal opinions ('unanimously that', 'questions of law'), license headers ('notice'), taxonomy stubs ('species of moth', 'gastropod'), and code. It is broadly a register/genre detector, not a specific token, and is hard to predict.

Fires on words for a quantity of money: 'amount', French 'montant', Norwegian 'beløp', German 'Betrag', 'sum', 'how much'. Also fires on ' in' after a money figure ('$40 billion in market value', '$11 million in funding'). Weak elsewhere.

Fires inside dates, mainly in non-English text: on the space or digits of the year after a day-month ('16 Nisan| 2017', 'juin| 2015'), on month names after a day number ('24| mars', 'novembre'), on 'de' in Spanish dates, and on year digits. Moderate on the comma in English 'Monday, January 16, 201x'.

Fires on the comma right after the first item of an enumerated list of nouns or names (e.g. 'Golden Gate Bridge, Alcatraz', 'electronic, mechanical', 'Mexico, Morocco'). Commas between clauses or later in a list fire much less.

Fires on formatting/separator tokens: '======' lines in Hacker News dumps, blank ' *' lines in code comment headers, and indentation. Also scattered prose tokens ('divergent', 'record', 'the'). The separator/whitespace part is the clearest; the rest is noisy.

Fires on function words and conjunctions in German text ('war', 'zu', 'dass', 'hat') and on 'Unless' in the Apache license boilerplate ('Unless required by applicable law'). Also fires on English function words in quantifier/partitive phrases ('size of', 'most of', 'one or both', 'not much').

Fires on a middle/second character of East Asian (Japanese) personal names (e.g. '小松[政]夫', '中島[哲]也'), and also on assorted subword pieces and hyphens in technical text and code diffs ('hel|ically', '10-k|b', '200|6-08'), plus 'I' in first-person lyrics. Mixed.

Fires on the coefficient or number right after an operator in polynomials ('s**3 -| 8*s**2', '+| 9*x'), and on prepositions or determiners that start a noun phrase in prose ('friend of', 'from that', 'in the', 'per fraction'). The two do not obviously share a cause.

Fires on the word right after a modal, a 'need/have to' construction, or 'that' in argumentative or expository prose, where a verb or complement must follow: 'have to [choose]', 'important to [understand]', 'need [something]', 'assumed [that]', 'drug [that]'. Weak on names and code.
